headline: Apple beat Wall Street and got marked down anyway, Mercedes can wrap up the constructors' title in Brazil on Sunday, and GTA 6 preloads open in nine days.

upcoming.what: UFC Vegas 124: Cortes Acosta vs Walker. Prelims 22:00, main card 01:00 Sun Irish time. England's Davey Grant is on the main card
F1 São Paulo GP qualifying, 18:00 Irish time (no sprint this weekend)
WEC finale, 6 Hours of Monza, 10:00 Irish time; F1 São Paulo GP 17:00; IBJJF The Crown from 18:00
UFC 334, Madison Square Garden: Gane vs Hokit for the heavyweight title (main card early Sun 15 Nov Irish time)
GTA 6 launches on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S at local midnight; digital preload opens Thu 12 Nov

items.headline: Apple tops estimates in Ternus's first quarter, but memory costs bite
items.summary: Revenue hit $114.48bn and iPhone sales $57.58bn, both ahead of forecasts, yet the December-quarter gross margin guide of 45-46% is down from 47.9% and Greater China missed. Shares traded near $329 after hours against a $338 close; figures come from a broker write-up rather than Apple's own release.

items.headline: Palantir nearly doubles revenue and the stock still slips
items.summary: Q3 revenue rose 96% to $2.31bn, US commercial sales climbed 148%, and full-year guidance went up again to about $8.5bn. Coverage says shares fell despite the beat, which sets an awkward mood for AMD and Super Micro reporting tonight.

items.headline: Nvidia reportedly in talks to back debt for an Anthropic data centre
items.summary: The chipmaker may guarantee billions in financing for Nscale's West Virginia site, which would shift some construction risk onto Nvidia. It is a report behind a paywall, so the exact amount is unconfirmed.

items.headline: OpenAI pools its limits, Apple Intelligence heads for China
items.summary: From December, eligible ChatGPT and Codex use draws on one shared allowance. Separately, Apple Intelligence begins developer testing in China tomorrow ahead of a December rollout, with Alibaba's Qwen handling some features.

items.headline: Update: the classified USSF-432 launch has slipped to Saturday
items.summary: Yesterday's brief had this Falcon 9 flying overnight, but one launch tracker now shows it moved twice more, to 00:46 Irish time on Saturday 7 November. It's reported to be another Starshield radar mission for tracking aircraft, cruise missiles and drones from orbit.

items.headline: Starship Flight 15 still has no firm date
items.summary: SpaceX hasn't announced one; Musk's early-October estimate of four to six weeks points to somewhere between now and late November. Treat yesterday's 12 November as a pencil mark at best.

items.headline: Physicists find a loophole that could let black holes split in two
items.summary: A pointer rather than a proper summary: ScienceDaily's article wouldn't load this morning, so all I can vouch for is the headline, dated 1 November. It was otherwise a quiet science morning from the sources I could read.

items.headline: GTA 6 launch logistics firm up: preload on the 12th, no disc in the box
items.summary: Digital preload opens 12 November, with launch rolling out at local midnight on the 19th on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S only. A launch roundup also says the physical edition contains no disc, and the base game is listed at $79.99 with Ultimate at $99.99.

items.headline: This week: Ocarina of Time and Stellar Blade land on Switch 2
items.summary: Zelda arrives on the 5th and Stellar Blade Complete Edition on the 6th, after World of Warcraft: Forever on the 4th; Football Manager 27 follows on the 10th. I found nothing new on Witcher 4, Cyberpunk 2, Witcher 3 or Borderlands, but most big gaming sites wouldn't load today, so that's a weak negative.

items.headline: Jaworski and Kapuścińska take double gold at European No-Gi
items.summary: Both won their weight class and the absolute in Rome, Paweł Jaworski with a heel hook in the absolute final and Martyna Kapuścińska with a foot lock over middleweight champion Injana Goodman. Britain's Nia Blackman won women's heavyweight on a referee's decision.

items.headline: The Crown brackets are out, with Mica Galvão at middleweight
items.summary: IBJJF's six eight-person brackets run on Sunday, also featuring Gabi Pessanha at women's super-heavyweight and Sarah Galvão at lightweight. It streams on FloGrappling from 18:00 Irish time.

items.headline: McNally goes from a Euro final to a Tonon rematch
items.summary: Sam McNally lost the featherweight final on advantages to Sergio Riquelme in Rome, and next faces Garry Tonon at Polaris 40 on 21 November. It's Tonon's first jiu-jitsu superfight in nearly six years, and McNally beat him on points at ADCC 2022.

items.headline: Fight week for UFC Vegas 124: Cortes Acosta a clear favourite
items.summary: Brady's withdrawal was down to a staph infection and Bonfim was pulled too, leaving Walker a +247 underdog to Cortes Acosta at -300 on opening odds. Suarez vs Jandiroba is also on the main card with England's Davey Grant, and I spotted no Irish fighters.

items.headline: Moicano won't appeal his disputed Halloween loss
items.summary: MMAmania's headline says so, with some choice words for the referee, but the article wouldn't load, so I can't give you the details of the stoppage. He had been booked against Tom Nolan at UFC Vegas 123 after Ortega withdrew.

items.headline: Mercedes can seal the constructors' title in Brazil
items.summary: They lead Ferrari 630-504 and need to outscore them by three points at Interlagos to make it mathematically safe. Antonelli will run a helmet marking the anniversary of Senna's 1991 home win; there is no sprint this weekend.

items.headline: Ferrari's Mexico fallout gets louder, and Russell's absence costs Mercedes
items.summary: Hamilton blames Leclerc's opening-lap aggression for handing away a likely win, with Vasseur also unhappy at the lost result. Mercedes were fined €5,000 after excusing Russell from mandatory media duties, and he has since issued a statement.

items.headline: WEC finale: Conway's last race, and how to watch Monza
items.summary: The six hours start at 10:00 Irish time on Sunday on FIAWEC+, with the #8 Toyota 17 points clear of the #7 and Mike Conway racing for the last time. I found no GT World Challenge Europe news today.
